=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer review

**Recommendation: do not accept the Seller’s update as a settled package.** It weakens recovery for core ownership risks, leaves significant completion liabilities unresolved, and attempts to shift disclosed and discoverable risks to Wattlebridge. The Seller’s statements about market practice and principal-level agreement are assertions, not evidence that Wattlebridge agreed to these terms.

The immediate priorities are: **(1) make Bluefen consent and its conditions a real completion condition; (2) repay and release Riverlark at completion; (3) protect the AUD 24 million debt-free/cash-free price from bonuses and other seller-period liabilities; and (4) obtain effective protection for Ironquay and the export incident.**

## 1. Liability and remedies

### Fundamental warranties and general warranty regime

The proposed **AUD 4.8 million cap**, 18-month notification period and thresholds may leave the Buyer undercompensated, particularly if they apply to title or capacity. A failure to acquire good title to 100% of Paperbark is not comparable to an ordinary trading warranty breach.

**Push for:**

- **Title, ownership, capacity and authority warranties** backed by a cap of at least the purchase price, no de minimis or basket, and a substantially longer claim period, ideally aligned with the applicable statutory limitation period.
- Separate, appropriate protection for **tax**, including a tax covenant or indemnity for pre-completion tax, with a period reflecting applicable assessment and limitation risks.
- Stronger protection for material **IP warranties** and a separate Ironquay indemnity. Do not assume the general 18-month period is adequate for ownership or historic IP defects.
- A higher general cap and longer general claim period than proposed, subject to negotiation and the Buyer’s diligence and insurance position.

The **AUD 25,000 de minimis** and **AUD 250,000 deductible basket** also deserve challenge. Under the draft, once qualifying claims exceed AUD 250,000, only the excess is recoverable—not the full amount. Seek a lower threshold and a *tipping* basket, under which the whole qualifying loss is recoverable once the basket is exceeded. Clarify aggregation of related claims and that the thresholds do not apply to fundamental claims or specific indemnities.

### Blanket limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance

The proposal to apply limitations and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions to **all claims of any nature** risks undermining the specific protections being negotiated.

**Push back** so each limitation applies only where expressly stated. In particular, preserve claims for fraud and other remedies that cannot lawfully be excluded, and ensure the provisions do not inadvertently restrict completion obligations, price adjustments, debt repayment, specific indemnities or equitable relief. Review the full SPA wording and applicable law before accepting any exclusion.

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

The Seller seeks to disclose the **entire data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records**, and to exclude claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could have discovered. Together, these provisions could neutralise warranties without identifying the actual risk.

**Push for:**

- Disclosure only of matters **fairly disclosed in sufficient detail** to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its relevance to the relevant warranty.
- Removal of blanket data-room and public-register disclosure; require a specific, indexed disclosure letter and a fixed, accessible disclosure bundle.
- Deletion of the “discoverable” knowledge standard. If a knowledge qualification is unavoidable, confine it to the **actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals**, without imputed adviser knowledge or a duty to investigate.
- Confirmation that disclosure and Buyer knowledge do not defeat **specific indemnities, completion obligations, price adjustments or express conditions**.

Specific disclosure still needs analysis: it may qualify an applicable warranty if the final SPA permits it, but it does not itself establish the legal outcome, loss or required remedy. Equally, the Seller’s reservation of liability does not resolve the underlying risks.

## 3. Bluefen — material customer consent

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, or 30%**, and its change-control clause includes conditions. No final consent or evidence that those conditions are satisfied is included. A reasonable-endeavours obligation and a rule treating consent as satisfied merely on delivery of a written consent are inadequate: the written consent could be conditional, qualified or commercially adverse.

**Push for a condition precedent** requiring, before completion:

- Final written consent effective for the transaction, on terms acceptable to the Buyer;
- Satisfaction or valid waiver of all associated conditions; and
- No material adverse amendment, termination right or cost imposed on Paperbark or the Buyer.

Require the Seller to procure this at its cost, keep the Buyer informed and provide the underlying correspondence. Include an appropriate long-stop date and termination right if the condition is not satisfied or waived by the Buyer. Review DD-002 and the actual consent wording before agreeing the condition’s precise formulation.

## 4. Riverlark debt and security

The approximately **AUD 3.2 million facility remains outstanding**, and no final discharge is included. A release after completion is inconsistent with a clean debt-free/cash-free closing and exposes the Buyer to repayment and security-release risk.

**Require simultaneous completion mechanics:** an agreed payout figure and lender payout letter; application of completion proceeds directly to Riverlark; repayment at completion; and delivery of executed releases/discharges, with any registrations promptly completed. The funds flow and price adjustment must ensure the Buyer does not economically bear the debt or pay twice. Check the facility’s change-control and discharge requirements and include accrued interest, break costs and other payoff amounts.

## 5. Completion bonuses and price leakage

DD-005 records **AUD 420,000 of conditional completion bonuses**, omitted from the draft funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. Although conditional on completion and continued employment, they are transaction-related obligations capable of reducing the value delivered to the Buyer.

**Require the Seller to bear them**, including applicable on-costs, through an explicit completion funds-flow deduction, payment arrangement or clearly drafted purchase-price adjustment, without double counting. Confirm which employees qualify, timing and tax treatment. More broadly, review the definitions of debt, cash, working capital and transaction expenses to ensure the agreed debt-free/cash-free economics operate as intended.

## 6. Ironquay IP

Transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of **every SOW3 fee**. The AUD 180,000 ledger entry suggests an open amount, but is **not independent proof of non-payment**; there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. A payment-only indemnity may leave the Buyer with the commercial consequences of an IP ownership defect.

**Before completion**, obtain evidence all relevant fees have cleared and a direct confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory confirmation from Ironquay. **Expand the specific indemnity** to cover losses arising from any failure or challenge to the Company’s ownership or use of the relevant materials, including reasonable defence and remediation costs. It should not be eroded by general disclosure, knowledge, basket or general warranty limits. Check the underlying SOW and whether other IP or third-party rights are affected.

## 7. Export/privacy incident

The unintended delivery of a link potentially affecting approximately **1,240 records** is unresolved. Access, scope, notification obligations and loss are not established, so it should not be described as a confirmed breach—but preliminary status is not a reason to leave the Buyer carrying the risk.

Require prompt investigation and preservation of evidence, including whether the link was accessed or disabled, what data was involved and whether notification is required. Seek a **specific pre-completion incident indemnity** covering resulting investigation, notification, remediation, claims and other recoverable costs, with suitable control and cooperation provisions. Require updates through completion and consider a completion condition or other closing protection if the investigation reveals a material issue.

## 8. Supplier renewals and other diligence points

- **Sandbar renewals — AUD 330,000:** The record does not establish that all three are unavoidable, accrued or ordinary-course costs. Review DD-008 and DD-011 together for dates, scope, termination rights and accounting treatment. Allocate any pre-completion accrual, debt-like item or transaction-related commitment through the price mechanics or a specific adjustment; do not deduct the full amount automatically.
- **Title:** DD-012 records the Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares, but is not complete verification of good, unencumbered title. Review the register and supporting corporate records, share issuances, transfers and encumbrances; obtain title warranties and proper completion deliverables.
- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a **notification obligation**, not an established consent requirement. Verify the notice timing and require compliance; do not manufacture a consent condition without reviewing the lease.
- **Mossvale:** The identified restriction is on **assignment**, not necessarily on a share sale. Check the complete contract and transaction structure before concluding consent is needed.

## Negotiation summary

| Priority | Buyer position |
|---|---|
| **Closing certainty** | Bluefen consent and conditions satisfied before completion; Riverlark paid out and security released simultaneously. |
| **Price protection** | Seller bears completion bonuses and applicable on-costs; verify all debt-like and transaction items in the funds flow and adjustment mechanics. |
| **Core recourse** | Separate, higher-cap and longer-duration fundamental protection; appropriate tax covenant and IP protection; resist blanket limitations and remedy exclusions. |
| **Known risks** | Obtain Ironquay payment/assignment evidence and a broader indemnity; investigate and specifically allocate the export incident. |
| **Disclosure** | Replace blanket disclosure and constructive knowledge with fair specific disclosure and, if necessary, narrowly defined actual knowledge. |
| **Complete diligence** | Verify supplier commitments, title, lease notice and Mossvale wording against the underlying documents. |

This review is based on the supplied Seller summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA or DD documents. The final markup should check the precise definitions, cross-references, funds flow and interaction of every proposed carve-out.
